source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 11 June 1949, p. 6 ("Notice of result of elections: Magherafelt Rural District, election of councillors, 1949 (Returning Officer's notice)"); Irish News, 20 May 1949, p. 3 ("Magherafelt Rural District nominations")
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Votes from the Returning Officer's notice, Mid-Ulster Mail 11 Jun 1949 p6 (page image read): Bates 10, Crossett 186, Malone 175; Crossett elected. Labels from the Irish News nominations, 20 May 1949 p3, which print Crossett (U.), the outgoing member, and Bates (U.), and none for Malone.

note: Triennial election of the 26 electoral divisions of Magherafelt rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. The Irish News prints the full nomination list of 20 May. Twenty-five members were returned unopposed; the Loup division was contested between Robert F. Crossett (U.), Andrew George Bates (U.) and James Malone, but no result for it was found, so it is not listed here. The Loup result, Draperstown (no nomination: the retiring member, Charles Campbell, deemed re-elected), Tobermore, Tullykeeran and Upperlands added from the Returning Officer's notice of the result (Mid-Ulster Mail, 11 June 1949, p. 6) (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026).
